issues.legal_issue: A decreed amount of mesne profits cannot be recovered through a statutory recovery process when the decree makes payment conditional on full payment of court fees and the deficiency remains unpaid.
material_facts: A decree awarded mesne profits subject to payment of court fees on the full amount, after crediting fees already paid.
The decree holder’s estate was taken over by the Custodian, who sought to recover the mesne profits through a statutory process.
The required court-fee deficiency had not been paid.
issues.conclusion: The Custodian was not entitled to recover the mesne profits under the decree while the required court-fee deficiency remained unpaid, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the decree itself made payment of mesne profits conditional on payment of the full court fee, so the judgment debtor’s obligation arose only when that condition was satisfied. The recovery mechanism invoked under Section 48 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act could not overcome the unsatisfied condition in the decree. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.statutory_recovery_of_decreed_mesne_prof: A claimant sought to recover mesne profits awarded by a decree through a statutory recovery process.
predicates.decree_payment_conditioned_on_full_court: The decree made payment of the awarded amount conditional on payment of the full court fee.
predicates.court_fee_deficiency_unpaid: The required court-fee deficiency remained unpaid.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks statutory recovery of decreed mesne profits, the decree conditions payment on full court fees, and a court-fee deficiency remains unpaid, the claimant is not entitled to recover those mesne profits.
